content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines introduction to django authentication as part of authentication, authorization, and user accounts. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Authentication versus authorization; Django's built-in auth system; Users and sessions; Password handling; Account lifecycle concepts. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Authentication versus authorization
items.text: Authentication identifies a user; authorization determines what the user can do. Prefer Django’s built-in password/user/session machinery and test account recovery and anonymous access.

items.title: Django's built-in auth system
items.text: For Django's built-in auth system, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: Users and sessions
items.text: Sessions associate server-side (or configured signed-cookie) state with a browser session. Use a suitable backend, expiry and secure cookie settings; avoid storing secrets or large mutable records in cookies.
